verdict.line: You lose trades and solo-kill races before level 6, but you win the head-to-head 53.3% of the time once Q stacks and Fury of the Sands come online.

brief.thesis: Irelia's Bladesurge (Q, 600 range, 10/9/8/7/6s cooldown) lets her dash in, strike, and heal, then reset the cooldown entirely if the target she hits is Marked or dies — so she can poke, stick, and disengage faster than your 255-range Siphoning Strike can punish. That mobility plus Ionian Fervor's stacking Attack Speed is why OP.GG gives her the lane and solo-kill edge, but it fades once your Q stacks pile up and Fury of the Sands comes online, which is exactly why the measured head-to-head still sits at 53.3% over 1260 games in your favor.

theirWindow.what: With Bladesurge up she can dash onto you or a minion, poke, and heal off the hit, then walk away before you land a second Siphoning Strike. Don't overextend for Q stacks when she's sitting on a full-charge Defiant Dance (W) too — it deals more damage the longer she holds it and reduces the physical damage she takes while charging.

yourWindow.what: Fury of the Sands (R, 120s cooldown, 400 range) gives you bonus Health, Attack Range, and drains nearby enemies' max Health into bonus damage for its duration. Walk up and force the fight the moment it's available — this is the window the 53.3% win rate is built on.

start.why: 53.4% win rate over 973 games and the 60.5% pick — the regen and damage reduction on the first attack blunt Bladesurge pokes while you farm Q stacks.

boots.why: 53.6% win rate over 763 games — directly answers the auto-attack damage Irelia stacks up through Ionian Fervor as the fight drags on.

core.why: First item in the highest-performing path (63.9% over 133 games) — the damage and tenacity-adjacent stats help you stick to a kiting Irelia.
Second item in that same path — the Attack Speed slow on nearby enemies directly cuts into her Ionian Fervor stacking.
Closes out the 63.9% win rate path — stacks your Soul Eater lifesteal with extra healing for sustained side-by-side trading.

situational.when: she is building into heavy on-hit or crit damage and you need the grievous wounds and armor
she is rushing an early all-in before your Q stacks or boots are online
you want the Spirit Fire-synergy slow zone instead of Frozen Heart's flat Attack Speed reduction

runes.keystoneWhy: The on-move healing and mana offsets Bladesurge poke damage during the early trades where Irelia holds the lane edge, and the highest-performing page (54.1% win rate, 52.3% pick) is built around it.

summoners.why: Highest measured win rate in this matchup at 55.7% over the largest pick share (47.1%) — Ghost lets you close the gap on or escape Bladesurge dashes, Teleport lets you reset onto the wave safely while you're losing the early solo-kill race.

playing.title: Don't walk up for Q stacks blind
playing.detail: If Bladesurge (Q) is off cooldown she can dash onto you the instant you step forward to farm a stack with Siphoning Strike. Check her Q cooldown before committing to melee range.

playing.title: Layer Spirit Fire under trades
playing.detail: Drop E (Spirit Fire, 650 range, 12s cooldown) on the spot you intend to fight in — the Armor reduction compounds your Q damage and the zone discourages her from walking through it to stick Bladesurge.

playing.title: Wither before she commits, not after
playing.detail: W (Wither, 700 range, 15-11s cooldown) decelerates her Movement and Attack Speed over time — cast it as she starts her engage so the slow is already ramping when she tries to dash or kite.

playing.title: Hold R for a forced fight, not a poke
playing.detail: Fury of the Sands only pays off if you're already in range to drain Health from her — pop it to start a fight, not to chase one she's already disengaging from.

playing.title: Freeze the wave before level 6
playing.detail: Since the lane and solo-kill data favor her early, deny all-in opportunities by holding the wave near your tower rather than contesting mid-lane trades you're statistically losing.

playing.title: Track her Ionian Fervor stacks
playing.detail: At max stacks her on-hit damage spikes — disengage or Wither her down a stack level before that threshold rather than trading through it.

playing.title: Use Teleport to skip the losing lane phase
playing.detail: If the lane is going her way by level 5-6, Teleport back after resetting rather than forcing more trades — your win rate comes from scaling, not from winning early exchanges.

brief.patchCaveat: Build, runes, summoners, and all win-rate/sample-size figures are measured from live games on the current patch via OP.GG; the mechanical reasoning and timing windows are my own read of the ability kits.

stats.opponentTip: Always keep your distance and pay attention to Irelia’s (P) and Conqueror stack count. Focus foremost on raising your [Q] stacks, and try go in for the kill post-level 6 when Unsealed Spellbook + Fury of the Sands [R] come off cooldown.
